LESSON: READING 3.2.1 READING FOR COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.2: Reading 3.2.1 Reading for comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 3.2.1 Reading for comprehension, part of Strand 3 in Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do you tell the meaning of a word from a text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. read a dialogue based on the theme for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 3.2.1 Reading for comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. infer meaning of vocabulary from a text for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 3.2.1 Reading for comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. seek to read texts for information based on the theme.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 3.2.1 Reading for comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. read a dialogue based on the theme for comprehension,

   Reading 3.2.1 Reading for comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. infer meaning of vocabulary from a text for comprehension,

   Reading 3.2.1 Reading for comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. seek to read texts for information based on the theme.

   Reading 3.2.1 Reading for comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. take turns to read dialogues related to the theme fluently,

2. answer comprehension questions based on the dialogues read,

3. work closely with peers to identify vocabulary items from the text,

4. create and fill word puzzles using vocabulary on the theme collaboratively,

5. work jointly to match the vocabulary identified with their meaning,

6. work together to use a simple dictionary to look up the meaning of the vocabulary,

7. collaborate with peers to roleplay a dialogue on personal safety.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. take turns to read dialogues related to the theme fluently,
2. answer comprehension questions based on the dialogues read,
3. work closely with peers to identify vocabulary items from the text,
4. create and fill word puzzles using vocabulary on the theme collaboratively,
5. work jointly to match the vocabulary identified with their meaning,
6. work together to use a simple dictionary to look up the meaning of the vocabulary,
7. collaborate with peers to roleplay a dialogue on personal safety.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 3.2.1 Reading for comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is developed as the learner engages actively when taking turns to read dialogues in

class.

• Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner engages in collective learning when collaborating to create and fill word

puzzles using vocabulary.

Values:
Unity: This is acquired as the learner cooperates with peers to look up the meaning of words from a simple dictionary.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and security: This is addressed as the learner interacts with texts related to the theme on personal safety.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate concepts on personal safety to their learning of similar concepts in Agriculture.

1. read a dialogue based on the theme for comprehension,
